Identify cell groups

identify.cell.groups.Rd

Builds, for each TF module, a dendrogram of the deconvolution features significantly correlated with it. The features are clustered on the value of that correlation: the distance between two features is the absolute difference between their correlations with the module (e.g. 0.62 and 0.58 are at distance 0.04). Two features are therefore similar when they are related to the module to the same degree (similar biological activity), not when they vary together across samples. The dendrograms are cut into cell groups by cell.groups.computation().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'cell.groups'
identify(
  relationship,
  clustering_method = "ward.D2",
  file_name = NULL,
  return = TRUE
)

Arguments

relationship

The list returned by compute.modules.relationship(). Its first two elements are used (accessed by position):

  • [[1]] (correlation): A matrix of correlations between TF modules (rows, named) and deconvolution features (columns).

  • [[2]] (significant): A list, named by TF module, of the features significantly correlated with each module (p-value, or adjusted p-value with padj = TRUE, <= the pval given to compute.modules.relationship()).

The correlations of each module are taken from the row with its name.

clustering_method

Linkage method of the hierarchical clustering (stats::hclust()) of the features on the distance described above. Default: "ward.D2".

file_name

Optional character suffix for the names of the saved plots.

return

Logical; whether to save one dendrogram plot per module to Results/Dendrogram_cell_types_<module>_<file_name>.pdf (Results/Dendrogram_cell_types_<module>.pdf without file_name). Each plot shows the correlation of every feature with the module next to its name, and its size follows the number of features. Default: TRUE.

Value

A named list of dendrograms (hclust objects, labelled with the feature names), one per TF module. Each one also stores the correlation of its features with the module (element correlation, used by calculate_dendrogram_cuts()). Modules with fewer than two significant features are discarded; NULL is returned if no module remains.

Examples

data("network.tuto")
data("deconv_subgroups.tuto")
rel <- compute.modules.relationship(network.tuto[[1]], deconv_subgroups.tuto[[1]], return = FALSE)
dendrograms <- identify.cell.groups(rel, return = FALSE)
names(dendrograms)
#> [1] "pink"      "yellow"    "red"       "blue"      "brown"     "turquoise"
#> [7] "black"     "green"
